memory_update.text: CGNX should be retained as the clean reference anchor for industrial machine vision, AI-enabled inspection, barcode reading, and factory/warehouse automation.

NOVT is a stronger underfollowed candidate for the edge industrial AI automation node because its precision motion, machine vision, RFID, and OEM design-in model can hide robotics and automation exposure inside advanced industrial and medical technology classifications.

ZBRA is a larger-cap reference/context candidate for physical-world automation infrastructure: RFID, barcode scanning, fixed industrial scanning, machine vision, mobile computing, AMRs, and workflow software.

OSIS is a speculative shadow candidate: relevant inspection and optoelectronic capabilities exist, but direct AI/industrial automation revenue exposure must be verified before promotion to a higher-confidence lane.

Layer 1C should explicitly verify segment-level revenue and backlog exposure to AI-enabled machine vision, factory automation, warehouse automation, robotics OEMs, and industrial inspection; current evidence is strongest for product relevance but weaker for revenue materiality.

node: Industrial and edge AI automation: sensors, machine vision, controllers, test/inspection, and robotics-enabling software
summary: Layer 1B expansion found one clear reference leader in industrial machine vision, one larger automation/data-capture anchor, and two underfollowed or shadow candidates tied to precision motion, OEM subsystems, inspection, optoelectronics, and industrial automation components. The chokepoint thesis remains plausible but not proven: real-world AI automation may depend less on models and more on deployable sensing, inspection, traceability, precision motion, industrial validation, and OEM-qualified subsystems.
